name: published-grader
title: Grade and score XP with the published grader
issue: Issue #71 (depends on backend grader-publish). PLAN (browser build, see notes).g. @bjorn3/browser_wasi_shim, exact pinned version) or a minimal hand-written one if the module only needs stdio/clock/random; call it the way verify/verify-graders.mjs does (grading request in, grading response with XP out). Load it lazily (dynamic import, never in the main bundle) from the bootstrap graders[] entry for the course language (grader/{lang}/wasi/v{ver}/manifest.json against the content CDN base), compile it in a Web Worker or with WebAssembly.compileStreaming off the main thread, verify the module's sha256 against the manifest, and cache the files in Cache Storage keyed by grader version (drop older versions). Prefetch at idle after bootstrap so the grader is cached for offline use; offline with a cached version grades normally; with nothing cached show a clear 'grading unavailable offline' state rather than failing silently. Grading and XP both come from the grader's grading response. Replace the callers in TypeInExercise.tsx, SpeakExercise.tsx, ExerciseRenderer.tsx, useLessonEngine.ts, LessonPage.tsx and SavedPracticePage.tsx; delete the TS grading port in src/domain/persian/ (typedAnswer, comparators, normalize, phoneticEngine and the grading parts of answerFeedback.ts; keep whatever is still used for display, e.g. romanization) and the XP stopgap src/domain/xp.ts + src/domain/xp-vectors.json. Do not change deferred-submit behaviour (PR #65 unconfirmed). Web CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml): a job downloads the grader pinned in a checked-in lock file (url + sha256) and runs the backend's published verify vectors and xp-vectors against it in Node (node:wasi or the same shim used in the browser, so the browser glue code is what CI tests).
acceptance: Grading and XP come from the published WASI grader, loaded lazily, cached per version, offline-capable
TS grading port, xp.ts and xp-vectors.json deleted
Web CI runs verify vectors and xp-vectors against the pinned grader; lint, tsc -b, build, test green locally and in CI
notes: USER DECISION 2026-10-10 (REPLACES every earlier note and the WASI/jco/preview1 parts of the plan): use the BROWSER build, the one Android runs, so web and Android share the same artifact and version stream. Reason: WASI is a preview-2 component, was about 100x too slow on Android, and Android dropped it; no jco, no transpile step, no WASI shim. Fetch grader/{lang}/browser/v{ver}/ (manifest.json lists files + sha256) from the bootstrap graders[] entry with variant browser, verify sha256, load lazily (dynamic import / script load, never in the main bundle), run it in the browser the way the build intends (its grader.xp(...) export and grading API: see tools/README.md in the backend repo and verify/verify-graders.mjs for the exact call shape), cache files per grader version in Cache Storage with offline support. Web CI downloads the pinned bundle from grader.lock.json (url + sha256) and runs the backend vectors + xp-vectors through the SAME browser glue code the app uses, in Node. A previous attempt may have left partial edits in the existing worktree (jco/WASI work was stopped before finishing): inspect, discard what does not belong to this plan, and carry on. Everything else in the plan stands (delete the TS grading port, xp.ts, xp-vectors.json; do not touch deferred-submit). REVISION 2026-10-10: nginx.conf is now an allowed path. The production CSP (all 3 add_header lines) has script-src self + Google GSI only, which blocks WebAssembly compile. Add ONLY 'wasm-unsafe-eval' to script-src in every copy of the policy (keep them identical). Do not add blob: or 'unsafe-eval' unless you can show with the real production-like setup (serve the built app with this nginx config or an equivalent CSP header and load the grader in a real browser, e.g. the claude-in-chrome or built-in browser tools, or a Playwright run) that the grader fails without it; if it does, stop and reply needsUser with the browser console evidence instead of adding it. Report what you verified in the PR body under Not verified if no real browser run was possible. Also confirm connect-src still permits the grader CDN host. REVISION 2 2026-10-10 (USER DECISION, supersedes every earlier runtime-fetch/cache/lock-file/blob instruction): NO runtime download of the grader and NO blob: URLs. The CSP stays script-src self + Google GSI + wasm-unsafe-eval ONLY (keep 6abb157). The grader is pulled AT BUILD TIME and shipped same-origin with the web build: a build step (scripts/fetch-grader.mjs, wired into npm run build and the CI build) asks the backend for the current published browser grader for the course language(s) (the bootstrap graders[] entry / the grader/{lang}/browser/v{ver}/manifest.json on the CDN: choose the stable way the build can learn the latest version without a user token), downloads every file, verifies each sha256 against the manifest, and writes them under the build output (e.g. public/grader/{lang}/v{ver}/ generated, gitignored) alongside the resolved version and manifest hash in a small generated file the app reads. The app loads the grader lazily (dynamic import / fetch from its own origin only, never in the main bundle) and keeps the offline copy via the existing offline/caching mechanism or Cache Storage keyed by version. No grader.lock.json pin: the build always takes the LATEST published version so web cannot drift; the resolved version+sha is recorded in the build output and printed in the build log. CI runs the backend verify vectors and xp-vectors through the exact fetched bundle and the same loader glue before the build is accepted. DRIFT/ROLLOUT: the web workflow must also run on repository_dispatch with event_type grader-published (the backend will send it, see backend item grader-web-dispatch) so a new grader triggers a rebuild and the normal deploy path; check how master deploys to production and make the dispatch go through that same path (if deploy happens only on push to master, add the minimal mechanism, e.g. the dispatched run rebuilds and deploys the same way; if you cannot make deploy work from a dispatch without new secrets, stop with needsUser). A browser run under the production CSP is still required: serve the build with the nginx config (or its CSP header) and load the grader in a real browser; report what you verified.
